  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Welch's correction for heteroscedasticity due to highly unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505) and heavy right tail (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81). Log transformation recommended given min>0 and strong right skew.",
    "For Success: One-way ANOVA is INAPPROPRIATE due to binary outcome. Use logistic regression with stimulation paradigm as categorical predictor, or chi-square test of independence. Alternative: Generalized Linear Mixed Model (GLMM) with binomial family and logit link, including Mouse as random effect.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Welch's correction due to extreme right skew (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) and heavy-tailed distribution. Consider robust ANOVA or rank-based methods (Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn post-hoc).",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Welch's correction or standard ANOVA if variance homogeneity holds; assess empirically. Right tail present (max=75.35) but less extreme than Path Efficiency.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA appropriate after confirming bounded [0,1] range; no transformation needed unless distribution strongly skewed. Check for floor effects given Sham mean=0.236."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violated if multiple trials per mouse; Mouse is a clustering factor (8 mice, 7233-10986 trials each). Recommend mixed-effects models with Mouse as random intercept.",
    "Normality: Assess via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk on residuals; expected violations for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and possibly Success (inappropriate for ANOVA anyway).",
    "Homoscedasticity: Critical concern due to 14:1 ratio in sample sizes (Combined vs Sham). Use Levene's test or Brown-Forsythe. Welch's ANOVA or heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors required.",
    "Outliers: Extreme values in Time-to-Target (201.39s), Path Efficiency (29.82), and Average Speed (75.35) may drive results. Winsorization or robust methods advised.",
    "Complete cases: No missing data (n=76655 for all variables)."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If Welch's ANOVA significant for Time-to-Target, Average Speed, or AD: Games-Howell post-hoc tests for unequal variances and sample sizes.",
    "If rank-based methods used (Kruskal-Wallis for Path Efficiency): Dunn test with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment.",
    "If mixed-effects model used: Estimated marginal means with Tukey adjustment on least-squares means, or pairwise comparisons with multiplicity correction.",
    "Specific contrasts of interest: Combined vs each unimodal (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and each stimulated vs Sham to assess additivity and efficacy.",
    "For Success (logistic/GLMM): Odds ratios with confidence intervals, multiplicity-adjusted pairwise comparisons via marginal effects."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham paradigm expected to show significantly worse performance: highest Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lowest Success (27.3% vs 67-78%), lowest Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lowest Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lowest AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40).",
    "Combined paradigm expected to show best or near-best performance across metrics, suggesting additive or synergistic effects of ICMS and visual stimulation.",
    "Unimodal paradigms (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) intermediate between Combined and Sham, with Bright Visual Only potentially outperforming Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only based on descriptive means.",
    "AD pattern (Combined highest, Bright Visual Only high, Sham lowest) suggests angular dispersion may index active sensory integration or exploration rather than purely 'better' performance.",
    "Group differences likely highly significant given large sample sizes and substantial mean separations, but effect sizes and clinical relevance require careful interpretation."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined: 48846 trials; Sham: 3505 trials) reduces power for Sham comparisons and inflates Type I error risk if not accounted for.",
    "Mouse as repeated measure: 76655 trials from only 8 mice creates extreme within-subject correlation unaddressed by standard ANOVA; pseudoreplication concern.",
    "Success as binary outcome violates ANOVA linear model assumptions; logistic/GLMM required but not reflected in 'ANOVA-style' framing.",
    "Path Efficiency extreme right skew and maximum of 29.82 (theoretical max ~1) suggests calculation anomalies or pathological trajectories requiring data quality review.",
    "No information on trial order, learning effects, or session structure; temporal confounds possible.",
    "Temperature=1.0 in metadata suggests possible LLM generation context; unclear if this affects data interpretation."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMM) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMM, binomial) for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect with 4 dummy codes (Sham as reference). Use Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite degrees of freedom, heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors where needed, and estimated marginal means with Tukey or Benjamini-Hochberg multiplicity correction for post-hoc contrasts. Report conditional and marginal R-squared, intraclass correlation for Mouse, and effect sizes (Cohen's d or odds ratios). For Path Efficiency, consider robust regression or rank-based mixed models due to extreme outliers."
}
